name: Cyberpunk & Dystopias
description: Questions covering: Cyberpunk Literature, Cyberpunk Film, Dystopian Literature, Cyberpunk Manga...

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel Neuromancer?
questions.explanation_correct: William Gibson wrote Neuromancer, a landmark cyberpunk novel first published in 1984. It helped define the genre's themes and style.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are notable science fiction writers, but they did not write Neuromancer. Their works belong to different titles and contexts.

questions.question: Who directed Blade Runner?
questions.explanation_correct: Ridley Scott directed Blade Runner, released in 1982. The film became a foundational work for cyberpunk cinema.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are major film directors, but they were not responsible for Blade Runner. Each is associated with different films and styles.

questions.question: Who wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four?
questions.explanation_correct: George Orwell is the author of Nineteen Eighty-Four, published in 1949. The novel is one of the most influential dystopian works in literature.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are authors of important speculative or dystopian works, but not Nineteen Eighty-Four. They each wrote different novels.

questions.question: Which superstate includes Airstrip One, where Winston Smith lives in Nineteen Eighty-Four?
questions.explanation_correct: Airstrip One is a province of Oceania, the superstate where Winston lives.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Eurasia and Eastasia are the other superstates; Ingsoc is the ruling ideology of Oceania.

questions.question: Who created Akira?
questions.explanation_correct: Katsuhiro Otomo created Akira, both as manga and later as an influential film adaptation. His work is central to cyberpunk manga history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are prominent manga and anime creators, but they did not create Akira. Each is known for different series and films.

questions.question: Who is the author of Brave New World?
questions.explanation_correct: Aldous Huxley wrote Brave New World, published in 1932. It is a classic dystopian novel exploring social control and conditioning.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are influential speculative writers, but they did not write Brave New World. Their works are separate titles from Huxley's novel.

questions.question: What is the name of the digital network that characters connect to in Ghost in the Shell?
questions.explanation_correct: The Net is the digital network to which characters and cybernetic systems connect.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are generic terms or names used in other fictional settings.

questions.question: Who directed Brazil?
questions.explanation_correct: Terry Gilliam directed Brazil, released in 1985. The film is a dark dystopian satire of bureaucracy and surveillance.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are acclaimed directors, but they did not direct Brazil. Each is known for distinct films in different styles.

questions.question: Which megacorporation is central to the Deus Ex series?
questions.explanation_correct: VersaLife is a major corporation in the Deus Ex series, especially in its conspiracy-driven plotlines. It plays a central role in the game's corporate power structure.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are major fictional corporations from other cyberpunk and dystopian works, but not Deus Ex. They belong to different franchises and settings.

questions.question: What is the alias of the anarchist protagonist in Alan Moore's dystopian graphic novel 'V for Vendetta'?
questions.explanation_correct: The protagonist known only as V wears a Guy Fawkes mask and wages a one-man war against a fascist government in Britain.
questions.explanation_incorrect: X, Zero, and Anonymous are not the identity of this character. The character's name is derived from the Roman numeral for five.

questions.question: Which corporation created the replicants in Blade Runner?
questions.explanation_correct: In Blade Runner, replicants are manufactured by the Tyrell Corporation. It is the company responsible for their design and production.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are fictional corporations from different sci-fi or horror franchises. They are not the manufacturer of the Blade Runner replicants.

questions.question: Who wrote The Handmaid's Tale?
questions.explanation_correct: The Handmaid's Tale was written by Margaret Atwood. She is the Canadian author of the novel.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are also major authors, but they did not write The Handmaid's Tale. Their works belong to different literary contexts.

questions.question: Who is credited with creating the Cyberpunk tabletop RPG?
questions.explanation_correct: Mike Pondsmith created the Cyberpunk tabletop RPG. He designed the game that later became Cyberpunk 2020 and related editions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are known game designers, but they are associated with different tabletop games. None of them created Cyberpunk.

questions.question: What is the name of the regime that rules Panem in The Hunger Games?
questions.explanation_correct: In The Hunger Games, Panem is ruled by the Capitol. It serves as the central political power over the districts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are generic political terms or fictional governing bodies from other settings. They are not the ruling regime in Panem.

questions.question: What is the name of the simulated reality constructed by machines to subdue humanity in the Wachowskis' 1999 film?
questions.explanation_correct: The Matrix is a neural-interactive simulation used to harvest bio-electric energy from humans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Grid is from Tron, and the Construct is the blank loading program used by the rebels.

questions.question: Who wrote Snow Crash?
questions.explanation_correct: Snow Crash was written by Neal Stephenson. He is the novelist associated with that cyberpunk work.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other authors are prominent cyberpunk writers, but they did not write Snow Crash. Their novels and stories are separate works.

questions.question: Who wrote Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
questions.explanation_correct: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? was written by Philip K. Dick. The novel later inspired Blade Runner.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other authors are major science fiction figures, but they did not write this novel. The title is specifically by Philip K. Dick.

questions.question: Who wrote Fahrenheit 451?
questions.explanation_correct: Fahrenheit 451 was written by Ray Bradbury. It is his well-known dystopian novel about censorship and book burning.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other writers authored famous dystopian or speculative works, but not Fahrenheit 451. That novel is by Bradbury.

questions.question: Who wrote We?
questions.explanation_correct: We was written by Yevgeny Zamyatin. It is an early and influential dystopian novel.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ayn Rand, Boris Pasternak and Mikhail Bulgakov wrote other works; none wrote We.

questions.question: Who directed the 1995 animated film Ghost in the Shell?
questions.explanation_correct: Ghost in the Shell was directed by Mamoru Oshii. He directed the 1995 film adaptation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are acclaimed Japanese directors, but they are not the director of Ghost in the Shell. Each is associated with different films.

questions.question: Who directed RoboCop?
questions.explanation_correct: Paul Verhoeven directed RoboCop in 1987. It is one of the defining cyberpunk films of the era.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are directors, but not of RoboCop. Each is associated with different films or genres.

questions.question: What is the name of the ruling political entity in Nineteen Eighty-Four?
questions.explanation_correct: In George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, the ruling political entity is called the Party. It controls every aspect of society.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are political-sounding names, but they are not the regime in Orwell's novel. They do not match the text's terminology.

questions.question: In Ghost in the Shell, which public security organization includes Motoko Kusanagi and her field team?
questions.explanation_correct: Major Kusanagi leads Section 9’s field team; Daisuke Aramaki is the chief of Public Security Section 9.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other unit names do not identify the organization in question.

questions.question: Which secret organization led by Bob Page appears in the original Deus Ex?
questions.explanation_correct: Majestic 12 is a secret organization led by Bob Page in the original game.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Arasaka, Umbrella and Tyrell are corporations from other fictional franchises.

questions.question: Clive Owen stars as which character in the 2006 sci-fi film depicting a world where humans have become infertile?
questions.explanation_correct: Theo Faron is a former activist who helps transport a miraculously pregnant woman to safety.
questions.explanation_incorrect: John Preston is the protagonist of Equilibrium, and the others are characters from different films.

questions.question: Who created Battle Angel Alita?
questions.explanation_correct: Yukito Kishiro is the manga creator of Battle Angel Alita. The series is also known in Japan as Gunnm.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are manga creators, but they did not create Battle Angel Alita. They are known for other cyberpunk titles.

questions.question: In Blade Runner, which city is the primary setting?
questions.explanation_correct: Blade Runner is set primarily in Los Angeles. The film presents a densely urban, rain-soaked future version of the city.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are major cities, but they are not the main setting of Blade Runner. The film specifically centers on Los Angeles.

questions.question: Which judge protagonist operates in Mega-City One?
questions.explanation_correct: Judge Dredd is the iconic judge protagonist of Mega-City One. He appears in the Judge Dredd comics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Anderson and Hershey are other judges in the comics; RoboCop belongs to a different franchise.

questions.question: Who wrote Snow Crash, the novel featuring Hiro Protagonist?
questions.explanation_correct: Neal Stephenson wrote Snow Crash, a 1992 novel featuring the hacker and swordsman Hiro Protagonist.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other writers did not write Snow Crash.

questions.question: Which corporation manufactures replicants in Blade Runner?
questions.explanation_correct: The Tyrell Corporation is the company in Blade Runner responsible for creating replicants. It is a central institution in the film's world.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other corporations come from different science fiction or horror franchises. None of them are the replicant manufacturer in Blade Runner.

questions.question: Which masked protagonist in 'V for Vendetta' fights a neo-fascist regime in London?
questions.explanation_correct: V is the protagonist of Alan Moore's 'V for Vendetta', known for his Guy Fawkes mask and vendetta against a totalitarian UK government.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rorschach is from Watchmen, Judge Dredd is from his own series, and The Joker is a DC villain.

questions.question: In Nineteen Eighty-Four, which superstate contains Airstrip One?
questions.explanation_correct: Airstrip One is a province of Oceania, where the novel’s protagonist Winston Smith lives.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Eastasia and Eurasia are the other superstates; Airstrip One is a province rather than a superstate.

questions.question: Who designed the Cyberpunk tabletop RPG?
questions.explanation_correct: Mike Pondsmith designed the Cyberpunk tabletop RPG. He created the game line that helped define the genre in role-playing games.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other designers are known for different tabletop games or systems. None of them designed Cyberpunk tabletop RPG.

questions.question: In the film starring Keanu Reeves as Neo, what is the simulated world used to keep humans under machine control?
questions.explanation_correct: The Matrix is a simulated world created by machines in which many humans live without knowing its true nature.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Grid is associated with Tron; the Construct is a separate loading program used by the rebels.

questions.question: Which corporation in Deus Ex is connected to the manufacture of the Gray Death virus?
questions.explanation_correct: VersaLife is a corporation involved in producing the Gray Death virus in the original Deus Ex.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options do not identify the corporation associated with the virus in Deus Ex.

questions.question: Who wrote Brave New World?
questions.explanation_correct: Aldous Huxley is the author of Brave New World. The novel is one of the most famous works of dystopian fiction.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other writers are well-known dystopian or speculative authors, but they did not write Brave New World. Only Huxley matches the clue.

questions.question: What is the cybernetic law-enforcement unit called in Ghost in the Shell?
questions.explanation_correct: Section 9 is the public security unit featured throughout Ghost in the Shell. It is the specific law-enforcement group referenced by the clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are generic unit names and do not identify the organization from Ghost in the Shell. Only Section 9 is correct.

questions.question: Which character, portrayed by Clive Owen, leads the attempt to protect Kee in the Alfonso Cuarón film 'Children of Men'?
questions.explanation_correct: Theo is an office worker who is recruited by his ex-wife to protect the first pregnant woman in 18 years.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Max Renn is from Videodrome, and Milo Thatch is from Disney's Atlantis.

questions.question: Which secret organization in the original Deus Ex is led by Bob Page?
questions.explanation_correct: Bob Page leads Majestic 12, a powerful conspiracy in the original Deus Ex.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Illuminati are another secret organization in the game; the other names are not the organization led by Page.

questions.question: What is the protagonist of Neuromancer called?
questions.explanation_correct: Case is the protagonist of William Gibson's Neuromancer. He is the key character driving the novel's plot.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are supporting characters or unrelated distractors. Only Case is the novel's protagonist.

questions.question: Who is the author of The Hunger Games?
questions.explanation_correct: Suzanne Collins wrote The Hunger Games. She is the correct author named by the clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other authors wrote other young adult dystopian works, but not The Hunger Games. They are same-category distractors only.

questions.question: What is the term for the android model in Blade Runner?
questions.explanation_correct: Replicant is the term used in Blade Runner for the bioengineered androids. It matches the clue exactly.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are general science-fiction terms for artificial beings, but they are not the specific Blade Runner designation. Only Replicant is correct.

questions.question: What is the name of the artificial intelligence system in The Terminator?
questions.explanation_correct: Skynet is the artificial intelligence system at the center of The Terminator franchise. It is the exact answer to the clue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are AI systems from different media or fictional settings. They are not the Terminator system named in the clue.

questions.question: What is the city called in Akira?
questions.explanation_correct: Neo-Tokyo is the rebuilt city in Akira and a defining setting of the story. It is the precise city name requested.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are cities or settlements from other fictional works or invented names. Only Neo-Tokyo is the city from Akira.

questions.question: Which Watchmen vigilante wears a mask with shifting inkblot patterns?
questions.explanation_correct: Rorschach is the vigilante whose mask features shifting inkblot patterns.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Comedian is associated with a smiley-face badge; Dr. Manhattan and Ozymandias are other Watchmen characters.

questions.question: Which Cyberpunk megacorporation is associated with Saburo and Yorinobu Arasaka?
questions.explanation_correct: Saburo and Yorinobu are members of the family behind the Arasaka Corporation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Militech, Kang Tao and Biotechnica are other corporations in the setting.

questions.question: In the dystopian film about a rigidly controlled nation, what is the name of the state ruled by the Capitol?
questions.explanation_correct: Panem is the nation in The Hunger Games, with the Capitol at its center. It is the totalitarian state that oversees the districts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are names of different fictional regimes or invented places, but not the nation in this film series. They belong to other dystopian works.

questions.question: In the cyberpunk film featuring a law-enforcement machine, what is the cyborg police officer called?
questions.explanation_correct: RoboCop is the cyborg police officer at the center of the film RoboCop. He is a resurrected officer rebuilt with mechanical components.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are related law-enforcement or robotic figures, but they are not the title cyborg officer. Some are machines or characters from different franchises.

questions.question: In the dystopian novel featuring constant monitoring, what device shows propaganda and receives information in many homes?
questions.explanation_correct: A telescreen is the surveillance and propaganda device in Nineteen Eighty-Four. It both broadcasts state messaging and watches citizens.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are communication or display devices, but they are not the specific all-in-one surveillance tool from the novel. They lack its exact function in the story.

questions.question: In Akira, which member of Kaneda’s motorcycle gang develops devastating psychic powers?
questions.explanation_correct: Tetsuo Shima develops powerful psychic abilities that drive the story’s conflict.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kaneda is Tetsuo’s friend and gang leader; Akira and Takashi are other psychic figures.

questions.question: In the dystopian film where citizens are chemically regulated, what is the drug used to enforce emotional conformity?
questions.explanation_correct: Prozium is the emotion-suppressing drug in Equilibrium. It is administered to eliminate feelings and maintain social control.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are fictional or generalized mood-control terms, but they are not the named substance in the film. They do not match the exact mechanism used in the story.

questions.question: In the cyberpunk television series, what term refers to the implanted backup of a person's consciousness?
questions.explanation_correct: A stack is the storage device for consciousness in Altered Carbon. It allows a person’s mind to be transferred between bodies.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are related tech-style nouns, but they are not the specific consciousness-storage term from the series. They do not have the same in-universe function.

questions.question: In Fahrenheit 451, what objects are targeted for destruction by the firemen?
questions.explanation_correct: In Ray Bradbury’s Fahrenheit 451, firemen burn books as part of a society that suppresses them.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Radios, instruments and photographs are not the objects targeted by the firemen in the central premise.

questions.question: In the cyberpunk video game clue, which augmented agent serves as the central protagonist?
questions.explanation_correct: Adam Jensen is the augmented protagonist of the Deus Ex series entry referenced by the clue. He is a mechanically enhanced security specialist.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are protagonists from different game franchises, but they are not the augmented agent in question. They belong to unrelated settings or genres.

questions.question: Which author wrote the cyberpunk novel Islands in the Net?
questions.explanation_correct: Bruce Sterling wrote Islands in the Net and is a major figure in cyberpunk literature. He is also known for shaping the genre's technical and political themes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are also science fiction writers, but they did not write that novel. Each is associated with different works and eras.

questions.question: Which director is credited with co-directing the 2012 film Cloud Atlas?
questions.explanation_correct: Lana Wachowski co-directed Cloud Atlas with Lilly Wachowski and Tom Tykwer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other directors are notable film-makers, but they are not the one credited for that film. Their careers are associated with different science fiction and genre titles.

questions.question: Which author wrote The Giver?
questions.explanation_correct: Lois Lowry is the author of The Giver, a landmark dystopian novel for young readers. She also wrote other books in the same loose series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other authors are famous for dystopian or speculative fiction, but not this novel. Their best-known works are different titles.

questions.question: Who is the central character in Nineteen Eighty-Four?
questions.explanation_correct: Winston Smith is the protagonist of George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four. The novel follows his life under the surveillance state of Oceania.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are protagonists from different literary works or are from a different genre entirely. They are not the main character in Orwell's novel.

questions.question: Who created Ghost in the Shell?
questions.explanation_correct: Masamune Shirow created Ghost in the Shell as a manga series that became a major cyberpunk franchise. His work strongly influenced later anime and sci-fi media.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other creators are influential Japanese artists and directors, but they did not create that franchise. Each is associated with different landmark anime or manga.

questions.question: Which megacorporation is the primary antagonist in Cyberpunk 2077?
questions.explanation_correct: The Arasaka Corporation is a Japanese megacorporation and the primary focus of the conflict in Cyberpunk 2077.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While Militech and the others are corporations within the game, Arasaka is the central antagonistic force.

questions.question: Who is the main character in The Hunger Games?
questions.explanation_correct: Katniss Everdeen is the protagonist of the original Hunger Games trilogy and its film adaptations. She becomes a symbol of rebellion against the Capitol’s rule over Panem.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are also dystopian protagonists, but from different book or film series. They are not the lead character of The Hunger Games.

questions.question: Which character is known as a highly skilled street samurai in Neuromancer?
questions.explanation_correct: Molly Millions is the street samurai from William Gibson's Neuromancer. She is famous for her reflex enhancements and combat ability.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are characters or terms associated with different contexts in cyberpunk or fiction. They are not the street samurai from Neuromancer.

questions.question: Which city is the setting of Judge Dredd's comics?
questions.explanation_correct: Mega-City One is the sprawling fictional city where Judge Dredd operates. It is the central setting for the long-running comics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other places are fictional cities or locations from other franchises. They are not the primary setting of Judge Dredd.

questions.question: What is the name of the police officer who becomes RoboCop?
questions.explanation_correct: Alex Murphy is the police officer who becomes RoboCop in the film franchise.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names belong to different science fiction or action characters. They are not the cyborg detective from RoboCop.

questions.question: In The Giver, what role is Jonas selected to train for?
questions.explanation_correct: Jonas is selected to become the community’s Receiver of Memory and begins receiving memories from the Giver.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other roles are not the assignment Jonas receives at the Ceremony of Twelve.

questions.question: Which AI is the primary antagonist in System Shock?
questions.explanation_correct: SHODAN is the rogue artificial intelligence that opposes the player in System Shock. She is one of the genre’s most iconic villainous AIs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are famous AIs from other works, but not the antagonist of System Shock. They belong to different franchises and settings.

questions.question: Which surveillance figure is used to represent constant monitoring in Orwell's dystopian world?
questions.explanation_correct: Big Brother is the symbol of pervasive state surveillance in Nineteen Eighty-Four. It represents the regime’s control over citizens.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices sound similar, but they are not Orwell’s term for the surveillance figure. They are generic titles rather than the specific concept.

questions.question: What is the name of the virtual world at the center of Ready Player One?
questions.explanation_correct: OASIS is the immersive virtual reality world featured in Ready Player One. It is the setting where much of the story unfolds.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are fictional-sounding worlds, but they are not the one from Ready Player One. They do not match the title of the central virtual environment.

questions.question: What is the title of Lois Lowry's novel about a controlled community and a chosen memory keeper?
questions.explanation_correct: The Giver is the title of Lois Lowry’s novel about a highly regulated society. The story centers on the transfer of memories.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe related roles or concepts, but they are not the book’s title. They do not identify the novel correctly.

questions.question: Which author wrote Altered Carbon?
questions.explanation_correct: Richard K. Morgan is the author of Altered Carbon. The novel is a major work in cyberpunk literature.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other authors are notable cyberpunk writers, but they did not write Altered Carbon. They are associated with different novels and series.

questions.question: What is the name of the protagonist in Altered Carbon?
questions.explanation_correct: Takeshi Kovacs is the central character in Altered Carbon. He is the key figure in the novel’s storyline.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are cyberpunk protagonists from different works. They are not the main character of Altered Carbon.

questions.question: Which writer authored A Clockwork Orange?
questions.explanation_correct: Anthony Burgess wrote A Clockwork Orange. The novel is one of the best-known dystopian works of the 20th century.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are major dystopian authors, but they did not write this novel. They are linked to different classic works.

questions.question: What is the name of the main delinquent character in A Clockwork Orange?
questions.explanation_correct: Alex is the protagonist of A Clockwork Orange. He is the central character around whom the novel’s events revolve.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are protagonists from other dystopian novels. They are not the character at the center of A Clockwork Orange.

questions.question: Which director helmed the 1998 film Dark City?
questions.explanation_correct: Alex Proyas directed Dark City. The film is widely associated with his visual style and noir-cyberpunk atmosphere.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other directors are prominent filmmakers, but they did not direct Dark City. They are associated with different science fiction films.

questions.question: What is the title of Alex Proyas’s 1998 science-fiction film set in a mysterious city where it is always night?
questions.explanation_correct: Dark City is the 1998 science-fiction film directed by Alex Proyas.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are titles of different science-fiction films.

questions.question: Who directed the 1998 anime series Cowboy Bebop?
questions.explanation_correct: Shinichiro Watanabe directed the anime series Cowboy Bebop.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are Japanese anime directors, but they did not direct Cowboy Bebop.

questions.question: Which series title refers to the 2006 cyberpunk anime set in a post-apocalyptic city?
questions.explanation_correct: Ergo Proxy is the 2006 anime series set in the domed city of Romdo.

questions.explanation_correct: Alfonso Cuarón directed Children of Men, a widely recognized dystopian film from 2006.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are major film directors, but they did not direct Children of Men.

questions.explanation_correct: Clive Owen portrayed Theo Faron, the protagonist of Children of Men.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other actors appear in many films, but they are not the lead in Children of Men. They do not match the requested role.

questions.question: Which studio developed the cyberpunk game Deus Ex?
questions.explanation_correct: Ion Storm developed Deus Ex, the influential cyberpunk role-playing game.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are game developers, but they are associated with different titles. They are not the studio behind Deus Ex.

questions.question: In the original Deus Ex, which AI assists JC Denton against Majestic 12 before merging with Icarus?
questions.explanation_correct: Daedalus assists JC Denton and later merges with Icarus to form Helios.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Helios and Morpheus are also AIs in Deus Ex; SHODAN is an AI from System Shock.

questions.question: Which artist drew the comic series Watchmen with writer Alan Moore?
questions.explanation_correct: Dave Gibbons was the artist for Watchmen alongside writer Alan Moore.

questions.explanation_correct: Black Mirror is the anthology series known for episodes like 'San Junipero' and 'Nosedive.'
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are dystopian or sci-fi television series, but they are not the anthology with those episode titles.

questions.explanation_correct: Altered Carbon is the Netflix streaming series featuring Takeshi Kovacs, played in its first season by Joel Kinnaman. It is the correct title.

questions.explanation_correct: Philip K. Dick wrote Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, first published in 1968.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other writers did not write that novel.

questions.explanation_correct: Arasaka is one of the major megacorporations in Cyberpunk 2077. It plays a central role in the setting’s corporate power structure.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other companies come from different franchises and settings. They are not the corporate entity associated with Cyberpunk 2077.

questions.question: What is the alias of the Guy Fawkes-masked anarchist in Alan Moore's famous graphic novel?
questions.explanation_correct: V is the mysterious protagonist of 'V for Vendetta' who wears a Guy Fawkes mask while fighting a totalitarian regime.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rorschach and The Comedian are from Watchmen, while Guy Fawkes was the historical figure who inspired the mask.

questions.question: What surveillance device is central to Nineteen Eighty-Four?
questions.explanation_correct: A telescreen is the two-way surveillance and propaganda device in Nineteen Eighty-Four. It is one of the novel’s most famous symbols of control.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are generic or from different fictional contexts. They are not the device used in Orwell’s novel.

questions.question: What is the common nickname for the multi-national conglomerate E Corp in the series Mr. Robot?
questions.explanation_correct: The protagonist Elliot Alderson mentally refers to E Corp as 'Evil Corp' throughout the series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cyberdyne is from Terminator, Virtucon is from Austin Powers, and Monarch Solutions is from Quantum Break.

questions.question: What is the name of the artificial intelligence antagonist in The Terminator?
questions.explanation_correct: Skynet is the AI system that becomes the central antagonist in The Terminator franchise. It initiates the war against humanity in the series’ backstory.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are famous AI characters from other works. They are not the antagonist tied to The Terminator.
